A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same harmonic-loss research. Their complete text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original toy experiments, five algorithmic tasks, MNIST classification and GPT-2 training and representation analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds loss comparisons, ablations, exponent sweeps, hidden-layer analyses, ImageNet training and SST-2/CoLA probing.

M1.justification: v1 Section 3 and v2 Section 2 define the same Euclidean-distance logits, inverse-power HarMax probabilities and negative-log-probability loss. The new component replacements and exponent sweeps are experimental controls, not revisions to the proposed method.

E1.justification: Appendix H adds ImageNet object recognition, SST-2 sentiment classification and CoLA linguistic acceptability. These substantially broaden evaluation beyond the retained algorithmic tasks, MNIST, OpenWebText and function-vector tasks.

E2.justification: Appendix D adds evaluated contrastive and spherical-loss comparators for MLPs and Transformers on lattice and modular-addition tasks. Section 6 adds component-replacement controls. Table 1 also includes published supervised-contrastive results, explicitly distinguished from the authors' own training results. The plotted labels establish comparator identities despite incorrect captions in Figures 10-11.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include ResNet-50 training with AutoAugment and top-1/top-5 accuracy, validation-F1 probes on GPT-2 layers 0 and 6, component-controlled experiments and exponent sweeps. The stated training settings for the original algorithmic, MNIST and GPT-2 experiments remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6 isolates Euclidean-logit and HarMax contributions; Appendix E sweeps exponents from 1 to 10 for MLPs and Transformers. Appendix C adds Block 6 parallelogram distributions and a capitalization case study. These substantially extend v1's modular-addition weight-decay study and coset analysis.

E5.justification: PCA aggregation changes from medians over 20 seeds to means, with added error bars. Figure 3 newly reports three-seed data-efficiency means, while Appendix F labels its corresponding curves fixed-seed. Table 2 adds ± uncertainty for probe scores. The uncertainty definitions and probe-run counts are not supplied, so additional runs cannot generally be inferred.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial ablation, sensitivity, hidden-layer and benchmark results. Under the authors' ImageNet pipeline, harmonic versus cross-entropy top-1 accuracy is 75.08% versus 74.17%. Probe outcomes are mixed: layer-6 SST-2 F1 ties at 79.9%, while CoLA is 77.1% versus 78.2%. Original MNIST accuracies and GPT-2 validation losses remain unchanged; algorithmic curves also reflect the revised aggregation.

T1.justification: v1 provides loss definitions, scale-invariance observations and an exponent-scaling heuristic. v2 Appendix G adds three formal theorems and proof arguments concerning finite minimizers, a PAC-Bayesian generalization bound and class-center representations, with explicit separability, bounded-input and margin assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims of improved interpretability, data efficiency and reduced grokking, including more interpretable GPT-2 representations. Explicitly describing the two existing loss substitutions clarifies the contribution without changing its scope.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly motivates compression and geometry as interpretability indicators and interprets the task-dependent contributions of the two loss components. Appendix C acknowledges that improved hidden-layer parallelograms coexist with heavier tails whose desirability remains unresolved. Appendices D and G add substantive explanations about alternative losses, class geometry and generalization.

D1.justification: Appendix H supplies implementation details for the new experiments: ResNet-50, AutoAugment, 90 epochs, an initial learning rate of 0.1 with specified reductions, and an MLP probe with hidden width 16. Existing implementation and hardware disclosures are retained; no new code or data access instructions appear.

R1.justification: Section 7 and Appendix D substantially reposition harmonic loss against contrastive, margin-based and spherical losses. New references cover loss surveys, supervised contrastive learning, generalization bounds and the linear representation hypothesis. Several earlier circuit and loss references, including Olsson et al. and Luo et al., are removed.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and experimental explanations receive localized revisions. Related work moves from Section 2 to Section 7 and its representation/mechanistic discussion is consolidated. Acknowledgements replace the impact statement. Much of the retained methodological and experimental narrative remains closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 changes from two-column to single-column layout, merges v1 Figures 4 and 5, condenses Figure 3 and places the full task display in Appendix F. It adds multiple analysis figures and two tables and corrects the grokking-axis labels. Some new captions are inaccurate: Figure 10 describes four ablation rows although the plot contains three alternative-loss rows.

improvement.justification: New ablations, sensitivity analyses and broader benchmarks substantially strengthen empirical coverage. However, Appendix G introduces serious proof gaps: joint input/weight scaling does not establish its fixed-input optimization claim, and Theorem 3 asserts an exact class-only convex combination while its derivation retains other-class terms and neglects them approximately. Incorrect comparison captions further weaken reporting. These empirical benefits and new reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of the net quality change.
